| `CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS` | Stall timeout in milliseconds for subagents. Also covers [workflow agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows.md#when-an-agent-stalls-and-restarts) on Claude Code v2.1.286 or later. Default `600000` (10 minutes); if you raise `CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` while the stream watchdog is on, the default rises with it, as [Handle slow or stalled API responses](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/typescript.md#handle-slow-or-stalled-api-responses) describes |
| `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` | Set the percentage (1-100) of the auto-compact window at which auto-compaction triggers. Use lower values like `50` to compact earlier; the variable can't raise the threshold, so values above the default percentage are ignored. It applies only in sessions that [compact before the model's context limit](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config.md#context-window-and-auto-compaction). Applies to both main conversations and subagents |
| `CLAUDE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_TASKS` | Set to `1` to force-enable automatic backgrounding of long-running agent tasks. When enabled, a [subagent](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background) moves to the background after running for approximately two minutes. If Claude queued a tool call such as a file edit behind the subagent, the subagent finishes in the foreground before that call starts. Also enables [automatic backgrounding of long MCP tool calls](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md#automatic-backgrounding-of-long-tool-calls) in non-interactive mode on Claude Code v2.1.212 or later |
| `CLAUDE_AX_PREPARK_MS` | In [screen reader mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/accessibility.md), how many milliseconds Claude Code waits before it writes a new or changed line. Default `0`, so Claude Code doesn't wait. Before v2.1.287, the default was `50`. Claude Code caps the wait at `5000`. Ignored in [project and local settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md#variables-claude-code-ignores-in-env). Requires Claude Code v2.1.233 or later |

| `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_BACKGROUND_WORKER_CHECKIN_SECONDS` | Removed in v2.1.283. Use `CLAUDE_CODE_WORKER_CHECKIN_SCHEDULE` instead |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` | Set the auto-compact window, how full the context gets before compaction, from `100000` to `1000000` tokens. Suffixed values such as `200k` require v2.1.304 or later. For precedence over the other ways to set the window and the effect on the status line's `used_percentage`, see [Set the auto-compact window](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config.md#set-the-auto-compact-window) |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_CONNECT_IDE` | Override automatic [IDE connection](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code.md). By default, Claude Code connects automatically when launched inside a supported IDE's integrated terminal. Set to `false` to prevent this. Set to `true` to force a connection attempt when auto-detection fails, such as when tmux obscures the parent terminal. Takes precedence over the [`autoConnectIde`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference#autoconnectide) global config setting |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL` | Sets the model for the classifier requests Claude Code sends in [auto mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode). Use a full model ID such as `claude-sonnet-4-6`. For the cases where Claude Code ignores it, see [Choose the classifier model](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes.md#choose-the-classifier-model). Requires Claude Code v2.1.302 or later |

| `CLAUDE_CODE_IDE_SKIP_VALID_CHECK` | Set to `1` to skip validation of IDE lockfile entries during connection. Use when auto-connect fails to find your IDE despite it running |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_IDLE_COMPACT_MIN_TOKENS` | Context size, in tokens, at which [idle compaction](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings-reference.md#idlecompaction) applies to a conversation (default: `200000`). Accepts a positive whole number, and anything else is ignored. Values below `100000` are raised to `100000`, the lowest threshold. Idle compaction is on by default for conversations that meet its conditions. To turn it off, set `idleCompaction` to `false`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.290 or later |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` | How many [subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md#concurrent-subagent-limit) can be running in one session before the Agent tool refuses to spawn another (default: 20). Accepts a positive whole number in plain digits; anything else is ignored, so the variable can adjust the cap but can't disable it. Requires Claude Code v2.1.217 or later |
| `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` | Override the context window size Claude Code assumes for the active model. As of v2.1.193, how it applies depends on how Claude Code resolves the model ID; see [Correct the window for a gateway or custom model ID](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config.md#correct-the-window-for-a-gateway-or-custom-model-id). Use this when routing to a model through `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` whose context window does not match the built-in size for its name |

| `MCP_TIMEOUT` | Timeout in milliseconds for MCP server startup (default: 30000, or 30 seconds) |
| `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` | Timeout in milliseconds for MCP tool execution (default: 100000000, about 28 hours). For an HTTP, SSE, or claude.ai connector server, each request also times out after 60 seconds by default; set this variable, or the per-server `timeout`, above 60000 to raise that per-request limit. A lower value still shortens the overall tool-execution timeout but leaves the per-request limit at 60 seconds. Stdio and WebSocket servers have no per-request timer. A per-server `timeout` field in `.mcp.json` overrides this for that server. A per-server `timeout` of at least 1000 also sets the minimum idle window for that server's tool calls, so `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` never aborts them sooner; this floor requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later. For the env variable, values below 1000 are floored to one second; for the per-server field, values below 1000 are ignored |
| `NO_PROXY` | List of domains and IPs to which requests will be directly issued, bypassing proxy |
| `OTEL_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMIT` | Standard OpenTelemetry SDK limit on attribute value length. Claude Code caps content-bearing telemetry attributes at the smaller of this and `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH`, so the truncation marker stays within the SDK limit. Claude Code reads the `OTEL_LOGRECORD_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMIT` and `OTEL_SPAN_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_LENGTH_LIMIT` variants the same way, and the smallest set value applies to all signals. Requires Claude Code v2.1.214 or later. See [Monitoring](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage.md#common-configuration-variables) |

If you set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to an [LLM gateway](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway) or another proxy, Claude Code gives each model it recognizes the same context window the model has on the Anthropic API. Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Sonnet 5 and later, Haiku 5.5, and Opus 4.7 and later get the 1M window with no `[1m]` variant to select, and a model that reaches 1M only through its `[1m]` variant, such as Opus 4.6, runs at 200K without it. Claude Code can't detect a lower limit that the gateway or the server behind it enforces. If your gateway rejects requests above 200K tokens, set [`CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=200000`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) in the environment that starts Claude Code, so sessions on every model [compact at that boundary](#set-the-auto-compact-window).

#### Turn off 1M context

>
> If Claude Code warned about the value of `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`, see [the variable's values and warnings](#claude_code_auto_compact_window-values).

You can set the auto-compact window in these places:

* **For one launch**: pass [`--autocompact`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference#cli-flags) when starting Claude Code. The flag overrides your saved setting for that launch without changing it, and `claude --autocompact auto` runs the session at the tuned window even if your saved setting has a value. Unlike `/autocompact`, the flag isn't preempted by a higher-priority settings scope such as managed settings.
* **In scripts and cloud environments**: set [`CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) to a token count such as `200000`. Unless Claude Code [ignores the value](#claude_code_auto_compact_window-values), the variable takes precedence over the command, the flag, and the `autoCompactWindow` setting. `/autocompact` then reports the override without saving. The status line's `used_percentage` measures against the model's full context window, so while the variable is set, that percentage doesn't indicate when compaction will run.
* **For one subagent**: see [Set the auto-compact window for one subagent](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md#subagent-auto-compact-window).

#### Values and warnings for `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`

A warning that quotes your `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` value means the value falls outside 100,000 to 1,000,000 or isn't a token count. To stop the warning, set a number in that range, such as `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=200000`. On Claude Code v2.1.304 or later, you can also write the number with `k` for thousands or `M` for millions, as in `200k` or `1M`.

A warning that quotes your `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` value means the value falls outside 100,000 to 1,000,000 or isn't a token count. To stop the warning, set a number in that range, such as `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=200000`. On Claude Code v2.1.304 or later, you can also write the number with `k` for thousands or `M` for millions, as in `200k` or `1M`.

Find your warning's wording in the first column, then read across for the window your session uses and what to change:

| :- | :- | :- |
| `reads as <N> tokens, so Claude Code treats it as the 100k minimum` | The smaller of 100,000 tokens and your model's context window | Set at least `100000`, such as `200000`, or `200k` if you meant `200` as thousands |
| `is too large, so Claude Code treats it as the 1M maximum` | The smaller of 1,000,000 tokens and your model's context window | You already have the largest window. To stop the warning, set `1M` or `1000000` |
| `isn't a usable size, so Claude Code ignores it` | The window from `--autocompact`, `/autocompact`, or `autoCompactWindow`, or the [default](#default-auto-compact-thresholds) when none is set | Set a number such as `200000`, or unset the variable |

| `reads as <N> tokens, so Claude Code treats it as the 100k minimum` | The smaller of 100,000 tokens and your model's context window | Set at least `100000`, such as `200000`, or `200k` if you meant `200` as thousands |
| `is too large, so Claude Code treats it as the 1M maximum` | The smaller of 1,000,000 tokens and your model's context window | You already have the largest window. To stop the warning, set `1M` or `1000000` |
| `isn't a usable size, so Claude Code ignores it` | The window from `--autocompact`, `/autocompact`, or `autoCompactWindow`, or the [default](#default-auto-compact-thresholds) when none is set | Set a number such as `200000`, or unset the variable |

A number with no suffix is read as that many tokens, so `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=200` means 200 tokens even though `/autocompact 200` means 200,000.
